_comment: The cinematic indie-film style of the Google Flow reel prompts, extracted from the owner's own scripts. src/agents/video.py reads this file: the 'film' block builds the same header for all three clips, 'worlds' says what is on the desk for each service (the default is the owner's oak desk and silver MacBook), 'vocabulary' is the camera/lens/texture/sound words the clips draw from, and 'rules' is the style guide the model must follow. Edit any text here; no code change needed. Every clip is written twice: a beat sheet (the director's version, 1-2 second beats with frame numbers) and a paste version (the header + 4 beats + one audio line) that goes into Flow.

film.stock: Kodak Vision3 500T film emulation with rich halation

default.set: a minimalist white workspace with a Nordic oak wood desk
default.light: a warm 3200K tungsten architectural desk lamp casting soft diffused shadows
default.cold: the cold, harsh blue glow of the laptop screen
default.screen: a sleek dark-mode interface with a subtle 'AR Designs' emblem in the top corner
default.props: a matte-white architectural lamp and a sleek studio microphone
default.texture: brushed aluminium, crisp glass reflections and volumetric dust motes floating in the golden lamp light
default.person: only hands, a fingertip, or a soft blurred reflection in the screen glass, never a clear face
default.signature: a single deliberate physical action that proves the idea, such as deleting one stiff sentence or closing the laptop lid with a soft magnetic thock

reel_scripts.screen: a script document where a stiff, robotic English sentence is replaced by a natural, conversational Hinglish line, with soft amber and teal pacing tags
reel_scripts.signature: deleting the stiff sentence in one clean sweep, then closing the laptop lid when the script is ready

chatbot.hero: a Space Grey smartphone standing upright on the desk beside the laptop
chatbot.screen: a chat window where unanswered message bubbles pile up in the cold blue glow, then tidy automatic replies appear one by one in warm green and white bubbles
chatbot.signature: the phone stops buzzing and settles face-down on the oak desk

animated_ads.hero: a Space Silver MacBook Pro showing a motion timeline, beside a single ceramic mug on the desk
animated_ads.screen: one still product photograph on a dark-mode timeline that gains soft keyframes and begins to glide, loop and glow like a finished animated ad
animated_ads.signature: a still photograph on the screen starting to move

website.hero: a Space Silver MacBook Pro beside a Space Grey smartphone on the desk
website.screen: a cluttered, confusing page that is rebuilt into a clean mobile-friendly page with a clear call button, shown on both the laptop and the phone
website.signature: a thumb tapping a clear call button on the phone screen

lead_gen.screen: a bright city map covered with small glowing location pins over shopfronts, next to a spreadsheet whose rows fill in one by one in teal and amber
lead_gen.signature: a spreadsheet row being added with each glowing pin

seo_blogs.screen: a blog draft with clear headings and short paragraphs taking shape on the dark-mode page, beside a clean search results page
seo_blogs.signature: a heading being typed and the paragraph under it tidying itself into place

camera_moves: rack-focus from the screen pixels to the glass reflection
horizontal slider tracking shot alongside the cursor
slight tilt-up with the centre in razor-sharp focus
texture: soft lens flare on the edge of the glass
tactile key presses and soft moving shadows
sound: a warm lo-fi ambient synth pad

rules: Show the benefit as ONE physical action the viewer can see (deleting a stiff sentence, closing the laptop lid). Never state it as a claim.
The person is only hands, a fingertip, the back of a head or a soft blurred reflection in the glass. Never a clear face, so the clips need no face consistency.
Name every object with its material, colour and state (Space Silver MacBook Pro, Nordic oak desk, 3200K lamp, matte-white lamp). Never vague words such as nice, modern or cool.
Light carries the emotion: the cold blue glow of the screen is the problem, the warm tungsten gold of the lamp is the relief. Switch from one to the other at the turning point.
Every beat has texture: halation, brushed metal, glass reflections, dust motes, bokeh.
Every beat names ONE camera move and ONE lens from the vocabulary. Clip 1 opens on the problem; the last frame of each clip sets up the first frame of the next.

Text on screen exists only inside the scene (a selection box, a short pacing tag, a small emblem) and is at most 6 words. It is an illustrative example sentence, never a claim about the owner's work, clients, prices or results. No caption or subtitle overlays: those are added later in an editor.

Audio is a timeline: silence, a first sound, a rhythm, a stop, a pad, a final tail. Few words are spoken; the visuals carry the rest. The voice is warm and conversational, like a friend sharing a secret, not an announcer.

The last clip ends on a locked, clean frame with empty space for typography and on the question the first line answers, and its sound fades back into the silence the first clip opens with, so a replay feels natural.
Story Feel is ONE line of inner feeling in Roman Hinglish (English letters only, never Devanagari).

arc.1: Tension and turning point: the problem is visible in the first second, then one decisive action changes the light from cold blue to warm gold and the flow begins.
arc.2: How it works: spot the problem, reject it with a deliberate action, a clean slate, then the better way appears and the person relaxes.
arc.3: Result and next step: the payoff, the one next step spoken naturally (DM keyword), a calm power move, and a lingering question that loops back to the opening.
